nodes.summary: Let $p \ne q$ be primes and $v$ a natural number. Then $\gcd(v, pq) \in \{p, q\}$ if and only if exactly one of $p$, $q$ divides $v$.
nodes.title: The gcd with pq is a prime factor exactly when one prime divides

nodes.summary: Let $p$, $q$ be primes and $g \in \{p, q\}$. Then $(g, pq/g)$ is a nontrivial factorization of $pq$: $g \cdot (pq/g) = pq$ with both factors greater than $1$. This connects the output of Rabin's algorithm with the factoring experiment of the library's public-key assumptions (`Cslib.Crypto.PublicKey.Assumptions.IsFactorization`, after Katz and Lindell, Section 8.2.3, citation as given in that module).
nodes.title: A successful trial factors pq

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and let $m$ be a square in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then For $m \ne 0$ this is Euler's criterion $m^{(p-1)/2} = 1$, since $m^{(p+1)/2} = m \cdot m^{(p-1)/2}$; for $m = 0$ both sides vanish. nodes.title: Square roots modulo a prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4)

nodes.summary: For all $n$, $d$ and $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, So an algorithm that inverts $E_{n,2d}$ (returns one preimage of each value in its range) also extracts square roots modulo $n$: a preimage $x$ of $m - d^2$ gives the square root $x + d$ of $m$. Rabin uses this with $n$ odd, where every $b$ is of the form $2d$ modulo $n$.
nodes.title: Inverting the Rabin function extracts square roots

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $b$, the Rabin function is $E_{n,b}(x) = x(x + b)$ for $x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. In Rabin's scheme the public key is $(n, b)$ with $n = pq$ a product of two large primes and $0 \le b < n$; the primes $p$, $q$ are the private key. Computing $E_{n,b}$ needs one addition and one multiplication modulo $n$, and no knowledge of $p$ and $q$. The function is four-to-one on most inputs,…
nodes.title: The Rabin function
